description.narrative: The project aims to reduce the vulnerabilities of communities in drought-prone regions through the implementation of anticipatory actions in WASH and Heath services.The Anticipatory Action activities for WASH services in the drought-prone population in Oromia, Somali and South Ethiopia regions. UNICEF will support the rehabilitation, preventative maintenance, expansion of existing water supply systems, water storage, and upgrading of generator systems to solar. UNICEF will improve WASH infrastructure in Health Care Facilities (HCFs) and schools in drought-prone areas. UNICEF will use pre-existing LTA and new contractors, minimizing contracting time. A number of rehabilitation sites have already been identified. For maintenance, as part of the water systems rehabilitation process, communities are capacitated to conduct basic operations and maintenance of their systems. Regional Water Bureau technical personnel will be oriented by the contractors during implementation of the activities of system troubleshooting to enable them to provide technical support to the served communities.UNICEF will provide WASH non-food items (NFIs), and materials to support Menstrual Health for women and girls, to the most vulnerable households in the targeted drought-affected areas. UNICEF will aim to reach 105,435 people (men 18,962, women 20,014, boys 32,751 and girls 33,708) with an estimated 21,068 people with disabilities with water supply interventions and hygiene, including 62,500 people (men 11,250, women 11,875, boys 19,375 and girls 20,000) with critical WASH NFIs and Hygiene promotion on diseases prevention and proper use of WASH facilities. The exact sites will be confirmed based on the needs, and availability of systems to be rehabilitated during the implementation. This project’s Health initiatives will focus on reducing vulnerabilities and preventing outbreaks among the drought-affected communities in the targeted woreda of Oromia, Somali, and SNNP. The worsening of the nutrition status of children due to drought, a high number of zero-dose children, and increased morbidities due to malnutrition and displacement could contribute to measles outbreak., UNICEF in collaboration with RHB and WHO will conduct an integrated measles vaccination campaign for children under the age of 5 ( U5) in the targeted woredas to response to the sporadic ongoing measles outbreak and prevent further transmission. UNICEF will launch an integrated measles campaign aimed at 444,557 Children 6-59 months of age in the 38 high-risk woredas. UNICEF, WHO, and EPI MoH, and EPHI are the primary stakeholders in any campaign, with UNICEF and WHO sharing responsibilities. For the planned campaign, UNICEF will handle vaccination management and logistics, as well as the communication campaign, while WHO would handle microplanning and HW training, with all partners responsible for M&E.
